1.explanation: The file src/languages/latex.js contains the definition of the MAGIC_COMMENT rule for LaTeX. Its regular expression currently matches only the exact casing “TeX”, so variants like “TEX” or “tex” are ignored. Making that regex case-insensitive (e.g. adding the /i flag or adjusting the pattern) will ensure all casing variants of “TeX” magic comments are highlighted correctly.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting LaTeX source, magic comments of the form “% !TeX … ” are recognized regardless of case by most editors. In highlight.js’s latex mode, the first line “% !TeX program = lualatex” is highlighted as a MAGIC_COMMENT, but the second line “% !TEX encoding = UTF-8” (notice uppercase “TEX”) is treated as a plain comment. The screenshots show the uppercase variant not receiving the special MAGIC_COMMENT styling. Magic comments should be matched case-insensitively.

2.explanation: The only place that defines the magic-comment syntax for LaTeX is in src/languages/latex.js (around lines 106–111). Its regex matches “TeX” with exact casing. That file needs to be updated (e.g. by adding the ‘i’ flag or making the ‘TEX’ portion case-insensitive) so that both “TeX” and “TEX” encodings are recognized as magic comments.
2.bug_scenario: The LaTeX highlighter’s “magic comment” rule only matches lines beginning with “% !TeX” in that exact casing, so “% !TEX encoding = UTF-8” (all-caps “TEX”) is treated as a normal comment. In most TeX editors magic comment keys are case-insensitive, so both “TeX” and “TEX” variants should get the same ‘meta’ highlight. The screenshots show: first only the lowercase “TeX” line highlighted, and second how both lines should appear.
